definition: Having no purpose or importance.
examples: His apology was meaningless.
Without you, my life feels meaningless.
These numbers are meaningless to me.

spanish.definition: Sin propósito ni importancia.

definition: The act of becoming impossible to find.
examples: The police are looking into her disappearance.
Nobody can explain his disappearance.
The disappearance of the plane is a mystery.

spanish.definition: Acto de volverse imposible de encontrar.

definition: The act of hurting someone who trusted you.
examples: His lie felt like a betrayal.
She'll never forget that betrayal.
It's a story of love and betrayal.

spanish.definition: Acto de hacerle daño a alguien que confiaba en ti.

definition: The study of the mind and behavior.
examples: She has a degree in psychology.
I'm taking a psychology class.
He's interested in the psychology of crime.

spanish.definition: Estudio de la mente y el comportamiento.

definition: Unable to stay still or relax.
examples: The kids got restless during the long drive.
I felt restless all night.
He's a restless young man who wants to travel.

spanish.definition: Incapaz de quedarse quieto o relajarse.

definition: A person who collects things as a hobby or a job.
examples: My uncle is a stamp collector.
She's an art collector.
The trash collector comes on Tuesdays.

spanish.definition: Persona que colecciona cosas como pasatiempo o trabajo.

definition: A medical doctor.
examples: You should talk to your physician.
She's a physician at the local hospital.
My physician told me to exercise more.

spanish.definition: Doctor en medicina.

definition: The state of being in contact with something harmful; public attention.
examples: Too much exposure to the sun is bad for your skin.
The hikers almost died from exposure.
The band got a lot of exposure on TV.

spanish.definition: Estado de estar en contacto con algo dañino; atención pública.

definition: A bad feeling toward someone because of something in the past.
examples: He still holds a grudge against his brother.
I don't hold grudges.
She has had a grudge against me for years.

spanish.definition: Mal sentimiento hacia alguien por algo del pasado.

definition: To shine with a soft light; a soft light.
examples: The stars on my ceiling glow in the dark.
Her face was glowing with happiness.
We sat in the glow of the fire.

spanish.definition: Brillar con una luz suave; luz suave.

definition: A ship that travels under the water.
examples: The submarine went deep under the sea.
He served on a submarine in the navy.
I ordered a submarine sandwich for lunch.

spanish.definition: Barco que viaja bajo el agua.

definition: Strong disagreement; the people or team you are competing against.
examples: There's strong opposition to the new law.
The opposition party lost the election.
The team knew nothing about the opposition.

spanish.definition: Desacuerdo fuerte; las personas o el equipo contra quien compites.

definition: A long rubber tube that carries water.
examples: He washed the car with a hose.
Turn on the garden hose.
Firefighters pulled the hose into the building.

spanish.definition: Tubo largo de caucho que lleva agua.

definition: A relationship between people or companies that work together.
examples: The two companies formed a partnership.
Marriage is a partnership.
They ended their business partnership.

spanish.definition: Relación entre personas o empresas que trabajan juntas.

definition: A person who travels into space.
examples: She wants to be an astronaut.
The astronauts returned to Earth.
An astronaut walked on the moon in 1969.

spanish.definition: Persona que viaja al espacio.

definition: To heat a liquid until it bubbles; to cook food in very hot water.
examples: Boil the water for the pasta.
The soup is boiling.
She boiled some eggs for breakfast.

spanish.definition: Calentar un líquido hasta que hace burbujas; cocinar comida en agua muy caliente.

definition: To go down on your knees.
examples: He knelt and asked her to marry him.
She kneels to pray every night.
The nurse was kneeling next to the boy.

spanish.definition: Bajar sobre las rodillas.

definition: Often dropping things or falling.
examples: I'm so clumsy; I broke another glass.
The clumsy waiter spilled the soup.
He's a little clumsy on the dance floor.

spanish.definition: Que deja caer cosas o se cae a menudo.

definition: Very fast.
examples: The company has seen rapid growth.
She has a rapid heartbeat.
There was a rapid change in the weather.

spanish.definition: Muy veloz.

definition: To give a good reason for something.
examples: How can you justify the cost?
Nothing justifies violence.
He tried to justify what he did.

spanish.definition: Dar una buena razón para algo.

definition: A plant with a strong smell, used for cooking.
examples: This sauce needs more garlic.
I like garlic bread.
Cook the onions and garlic in a little oil.

spanish.definition: Planta de olor fuerte que se usa para cocinar.

definition: Bullets and other things fired from guns.
examples: The soldiers ran out of ammunition.
He bought ammunition for his rifle.
They found guns and ammunition in the car.

spanish.definition: Balas y otras cosas que se disparan con armas.

definition: An explanation of what a word means.
examples: Look up the definition in the dictionary.
What's the definition of this word?
This word has more than one definition.

spanish.definition: Explicación de lo que significa una palabra.

definition: To tell someone something officially.
examples: Please notify us if you move.
The school notified the parents.
We'll notify you when your order arrives.

spanish.definition: Decirle algo a alguien de forma oficial.

definition: The way something is arranged; a trick to make someone look guilty.
examples: I love your office setup.
The setup of the new computer took an hour.
It's a setup! I didn't take the money.

spanish.definition: Manera en que algo está organizado; truco para hacer ver culpable a alguien.

definition: Having bad luck.
examples: Some people think thirteen is an unlucky number.
He was unlucky to lose the game.
I'm always unlucky at cards.

spanish.definition: Que tiene mala suerte.

definition: A room where students have lessons.
examples: The teacher walked into the classroom.
Our classroom has twenty desks.
No phones are allowed in the classroom.

spanish.definition: Cuarto donde los estudiantes tienen clases.

definition: A formal agreement between countries.
examples: The two countries signed a peace treaty.
The treaty ended the war.
The president broke the treaty.

spanish.definition: Acuerdo formal entre países.

definition: To take a long walk in nature; a long walk in nature.
examples: We went for a hike in the mountains.
I love to hike on weekends.
They hiked for six hours.

spanish.definition: Dar una caminata larga en la naturaleza; caminata larga en la naturaleza.

definition: The long line of bones in the middle of your back.
examples: He hurt his spine in the accident.
She had surgery on her spine.
Sit up and keep your spine straight.

spanish.definition: Línea larga de huesos en el medio de la espalda.

definition: To notice or discover something.
examples: This machine can detect metal.
I detect a little anger in your voice.
The test detected the disease early.

spanish.definition: Notar o descubrir algo.

definition: To laugh at someone in an unkind way; not real, but made for practice.
examples: Stop mocking me.
The other kids mocked his accent.
We did a mock interview to practice.

spanish.definition: Reírse de alguien de forma cruel; que no es real sino hecho para practicar.

definition: A place where people get their hair or nails done.
examples: She works at a hair salon.
I have an appointment at the salon.
They opened a nail salon downtown.

spanish.definition: Lugar donde la gente se arregla el pelo o las uñas.

definition: A good quality in a person.
examples: Patience is a virtue.
Honesty is his greatest virtue.
She talked about the virtues of hard work.

spanish.definition: Buena cualidad de una persona.

definition: A case brought to a court by a person or a company.
examples: They filed a lawsuit against the hospital.
She won the lawsuit.
The company is facing a big lawsuit.

spanish.definition: Caso llevado a un juzgado por una persona o empresa.

definition: To hit your hands together, often to show you like something.
examples: Everyone clapped at the end of the song.
The kids were clapping and singing.
Clap your hands if you're happy.

spanish.definition: Golpear las manos, a menudo para mostrar que algo te gusta.

definition: Hair that grows above a man's top lip.
examples: My dad has a big gray mustache.
He shaved off his mustache.
You'd look funny with a mustache.

spanish.definition: Pelo que crece sobre el labio de arriba de un hombre.

definition: A place people like to visit; a feeling of liking someone.
examples: The Statue of Liberty is a big tourist attraction.
There was an instant attraction between them.
The main attraction at the fair was the roller coaster.

spanish.definition: Lugar que a la gente le gusta visitar; sentimiento de gustarte alguien.

definition: To remove the skin of a fruit or vegetable; the skin of a fruit.
examples: Peel the potatoes before you cook them.
He peeled an orange.
Don't throw the banana peel on the floor.

spanish.definition: Quitar la piel de una fruta o verdura; piel de una fruta.

definition: Something or someone useful; something valuable that you own.
examples: She's a great asset to our team.
His house is his biggest asset.
The company sold some of its assets.

spanish.definition: Algo o alguien útil; algo valioso que posees.

definition: A class where people learn by doing; a room where things are made or fixed.
examples: I went to a writing workshop.
He builds furniture in his workshop.
The workshop lasts two days.

spanish.definition: Clase donde se aprende haciendo; cuarto donde se hacen o arreglan cosas.

definition: To become bigger, or to make something bigger.
examples: The company plans to expand next year.
Metal expands when it gets hot.
Reading expands your mind.

spanish.definition: Volverse más grande, o hacer algo más grande.

definition: The time in the morning when the sun comes up.
examples: We got up early to watch the sunrise.
The farmers start work at sunrise.
The sunrise over the ocean was beautiful.

spanish.definition: Momento de la mañana en que sale el sol.

definition: A round, sweet fruit with soft skin.
examples: I ate a sweet peach.
She makes a great peach pie.
Georgia is famous for its peaches.

spanish.definition: Fruta redonda y dulce de piel suave.

definition: A group of things to choose from; the act of choosing.
examples: This store has a great selection of shoes.
The selection of the new team starts soon.
They offer a wide selection of wines.

spanish.definition: Grupo de cosas para elegir; acto de elegir.

definition: Next to something; together with someone.
examples: We walked alongside the river.
I work alongside my brother.
A truck pulled up alongside our car.

spanish.definition: Al lado de algo; junto con alguien.

definition: Connected to a system where people vote for their leaders.
examples: It's a free and democratic country.
They held democratic elections.
The decision was made in a democratic way.

spanish.definition: Relacionado con un sistema donde la gente vota por sus líderes.

definition: A dishonest person.
examples: That car salesman is a crook.
The crooks stole all of his money.
Don't trust him. He's a crook.

spanish.definition: Persona deshonesta.

definition: To hold something firmly; to understand something.
examples: She grasped his hand.
He has a good grasp of English.
I can't grasp this idea.

spanish.definition: Sostener algo con fuerza; entender algo.

definition: To change words from one language to another.
examples: Can you translate this letter into Spanish?
She translates books for a living.
I translated the menu for my parents.

spanish.definition: Cambiar palabras de un idioma a otro.

definition: Very strong anger.
examples: His eyes were full of fury.
She shouted at him in fury.
They felt the fury of the storm.

spanish.definition: Rabia muy fuerte.

definition: A place where soldiers fight.
examples: Thousands of men died on the battlefield.
We visited the Gettysburg battlefield.
He was hurt on the battlefield.

spanish.definition: Lugar donde pelean los soldados.

definition: Covered in something that makes things stick to it.
examples: My hands are sticky from the candy.
The table is sticky.
I left you a sticky note.

spanish.definition: Cubierto de algo que hace que las cosas se peguen.

definition: Very simple; from a very early time.
examples: They used primitive tools.
The cabin has primitive toilets.
Primitive people lived in caves.

spanish.definition: Muy simple; de una época muy antigua.

definition: The time when a king or queen rules; to rule as a king or queen.
examples: The queen's reign lasted seventy years.
He reigned for twenty years.
The country grew rich during his reign.

spanish.definition: Tiempo en que gobierna un rey o una reina; gobernar como rey o reina.

definition: To hide something in a secret place; a hidden group of things.
examples: He stashed the money under his bed.
I found her stash of chocolate.
She's stashing cash for her trip.

spanish.definition: Guardar algo en un lugar secreto; grupo de cosas escondidas.

definition: To open something with a key or a code.
examples: I can't unlock my phone.
She unlocked the door.
Use this key to unlock the box.

spanish.definition: Abrir algo con una llave o un código.

definition: Strange or unusual.
examples: There's a peculiar smell in here.
He has a peculiar way of talking.
What a peculiar old house!

spanish.definition: Raro o poco común.

definition: A plant with a fresh taste; a small candy with this taste.
examples: Would you like a mint?
I put fresh mint in my tea.
This toothpaste tastes like mint.

spanish.definition: Planta de sabor fresco; dulce pequeño con este sabor.

definition: A small safety part in an electric system.
examples: The lights went out because a fuse blew.
We need to replace the fuse.
He lit the fuse and ran away.

spanish.definition: Pequeña parte de seguridad en un sistema eléctrico.

definition: Money or property you get from someone who has died.
examples: She got a large inheritance from her aunt.
They fought over the inheritance.
He spent his inheritance on a house.

spanish.definition: Dinero o propiedad que recibes de alguien que murió.

definition: The act of knowing who someone is; praise for what you did.
examples: She got recognition for her work.
The phone has facial recognition.
He deserves more recognition.

spanish.definition: Acto de saber quién es alguien; elogio por lo que hiciste.

definition: A tool for digging; to move something with this tool.
examples: He dug the hole with a shovel.
I had to shovel snow this morning.
The kids brought a bucket and a shovel to the beach.

spanish.definition: Herramienta para cavar; mover algo con esta herramienta.

definition: Good at art or connected to art.
examples: She's a very artistic child.
He has artistic talent.
The photos have an artistic style.

spanish.definition: Bueno para el arte o relacionado con el arte.

definition: A boat that carries people and cars across water.
examples: We took the ferry to the island.
The ferry leaves every hour.
You can see the city from the ferry.

spanish.definition: Barco que lleva personas y carros a través del agua.

definition: Connected to atoms or to the energy they produce.
examples: They dropped an atomic bomb in 1945.
He studies atomic energy.
An atomic clock is very exact.

spanish.definition: Relacionado con los átomos o la energía que producen.

definition: Trying to protect yourself; acting as if someone is attacking you.
examples: Why are you so defensive?
He's the best defensive player on the team.
She got defensive when I asked about the money.

spanish.definition: Que trata de protegerse; que actúa como si alguien te atacara.

definition: A physical feeling; something that causes great excitement.
examples: I have a burning sensation in my leg.
The new singer is a sensation.
She felt a strange sensation in her stomach.

spanish.definition: Sentimiento físico; algo que causa gran emoción.

definition: A person who is running from the police.
examples: The fugitive was caught in Mexico.
Police are looking for two fugitives.
He lived as a fugitive for years.

spanish.definition: Persona que huye de la policía.

definition: Connected to a city.
examples: More people live in urban areas now.
Urban life can be stressful.
The school is in an urban neighborhood.

spanish.definition: Relacionado con una ciudad.

definition: Great care to avoid danger.
examples: Drive with caution on icy roads.
Use caution when you open the door.
We need to treat this with caution.

spanish.definition: Gran cuidado para evitar el peligro.

definition: Complete and careful.
examples: The police did a thorough search.
She's very thorough in her work.
The room needs a thorough cleaning.

spanish.definition: Completo y cuidadoso.

definition: Neat and in order; to make a place neat.
examples: Her room is always tidy.
Please tidy up before dinner.
He tidied his desk and went home.

spanish.definition: Limpio y en orden; poner un lugar en orden.

definition: Something you must do.
examples: You have no obligation to buy anything.
Parents have an obligation to care for their kids.
I felt an obligation to help.

spanish.definition: Algo que debes hacer.

definition: To send back light or an image; to think carefully.
examples: The mirror reflects your face.
The lake reflected the mountains.
I need some time to reflect on this.

spanish.definition: Devolver la luz o una imagen; pensar con cuidado.

definition: The part of a shirt or jacket that covers your arm.
examples: He rolled up his sleeves.
The shirt has long sleeves.
There's a hole in my sleeve.

spanish.definition: Parte de una camisa o chaqueta que cubre el brazo.

definition: Stylish and of high quality.
examples: That's a very classy restaurant.
She wore a classy black dress.
He's a classy guy.

spanish.definition: Con estilo y de alta calidad.

definition: A statement or proof that something is true or will happen.
examples: I got an email confirmation of my order.
We're waiting for confirmation of the news.
The hotel sent me a confirmation number.

spanish.definition: Declaración o prueba de que algo es verdad o va a pasar.

definition: A person who has at least a million dollars.
examples: He became a millionaire at thirty.
I'd love to be a millionaire.
The millionaire gave money to the hospital.

spanish.definition: Persona que tiene al menos un millón de dólares.

definition: The act of legally taking a child into your family.
examples: They chose adoption after years of trying.
The adoption took two years.
The shelter has many dogs for adoption.

spanish.definition: Acto de tomar legalmente a un niño en tu familia.

definition: A bright object in space with a long tail.
examples: We saw a comet in the night sky.
This comet comes back every seventy-six years.
The comet's tail was very long.

spanish.definition: Objeto brillante del espacio con una cola larga.

definition: Good enough; allowed.
examples: Your work is acceptable.
That kind of behavior isn't acceptable.
Is it acceptable to wear jeans to work?

spanish.definition: Suficientemente bueno; permitido.

definition: Practical and based on what is possible; looking real.
examples: We need a realistic plan.
Let's be realistic about the cost.
The painting is very realistic.

spanish.definition: Práctico y basado en lo que es posible; que parece real.

definition: Enough.
examples: We have sufficient food for the trip.
There wasn't sufficient evidence.
One bottle should be sufficient.

spanish.definition: Bastante.

definition: Connected to the mind and to thinking; a person who studies and thinks a lot.
examples: He's an intellectual man.
She enjoys intellectual conversations.
Many intellectuals came to the talk.

spanish.definition: Relacionado con la mente y el pensamiento; persona que estudia y piensa mucho.

definition: To throw up food from your stomach.
examples: The child vomited in the car.
I felt like I was going to vomit.
There was vomit on the floor.

spanish.definition: Sacar la comida del estómago por la boca.

definition: The state of being warm; a friendly feeling.
examples: We sat near the fire for warmth.
I love the warmth of the sun.
She greeted us with great warmth.

spanish.definition: Estado de estar tibio; sentimiento amistoso.

definition: To make someone upset or angry.
examples: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.
His joke offended a lot of people.
She's easily offended.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien se moleste o se enoje.

definition: A machine that keeps food cold.
examples: Put the milk in the refrigerator.
Our refrigerator is empty.
There's some chicken in the refrigerator.

spanish.definition: Máquina que mantiene fría la comida.

definition: A person who teaches a skill.
examples: My driving instructor is very patient.
She's a yoga instructor.
The ski instructor showed us how to stop.

spanish.definition: Persona que enseña una habilidad.

definition: Extra hours at work; extra time in a game.
examples: He works overtime on weekends.
We get paid extra for overtime.
The game went into overtime.

spanish.definition: Horas adicionales en el trabajo; tiempo adicional en un juego.

definition: To move slowly, carried by water or air.
examples: The boat drifted away from the shore.
We drifted apart after high school.
Clouds were drifting across the sky.

spanish.definition: Moverse lento, llevado por el agua o el aire.

definition: A very bad end that you cannot stop.
examples: The ship sailed to its doom.
He felt a sense of doom.
Stop talking about doom and disaster.

spanish.definition: Final muy malo que no puedes detener.

definition: A narrow path between rows of seats or shelves.
examples: Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat?
The rice is in aisle five.
She walked down the aisle with her father.

spanish.definition: Camino estrecho entre filas de sillas o estantes.

definition: One version of a book, magazine, or newspaper.
examples: This is the third edition of the book.
I read the Sunday edition of the paper.
The game comes in a special edition.

spanish.definition: Versión de un libro, una revista o un periódico.

definition: To show how something works; to protest in public.
examples: Let me demonstrate how to use it.
The results demonstrate that it works.
Workers demonstrated in the streets.

spanish.definition: Mostrar cómo funciona algo; protestar en público.

definition: A poor person who asks people for money or food.
examples: A beggar asked me for some change.
She gave a dollar to the beggar.
There are beggars outside the train station.

spanish.definition: Persona pobre que le pide dinero o comida a la gente.

definition: To make something start working.
examples: You need to activate your new card.
The alarm is activated by smoke.
I'm activating my account now.

spanish.definition: Hacer que algo empiece a funcionar.

definition: Very brave.
examples: It was a heroic rescue.
The firefighters made a heroic effort.
He died in a heroic way.

spanish.definition: Muy valiente.

definition: A funny drawing; a movie or TV show made with drawings.
examples: My kids watch cartoons on Saturday morning.
There's a funny cartoon in the newspaper.
Which cartoon was your favorite when you were little?

spanish.definition: Dibujo chistoso; película o programa de TV hecho con dibujos.
